---
engine: markdown
title: "JSON / JSONL"
---

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

Files ending in `.json` are read with `jsonlite::fromJSON()`; `.jsonl` and
`.ndjson` files (JSON Lines, one object per line) are read line by line with
`jsonlite::stream_in()`. Write JSON with `-O json` or an output file ending
in `.json`, and JSON Lines with `-O jsonl` or `.jsonl`.

## Reading JSON

An array of objects becomes a data frame with a row per object:

```{term}
echo '[{"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "city": "Amsterdam"},
       {"name": "Bob", "age": 25, "city": "Rotterdam"},
       {"name": "Carol", "age": 35, "city": "Utrecht"}]' > people.json
rush run 'dplyr::filter(df, age > 28)' people.json
```

## Writing JSON

```{term}
rush run -O json 'head(df[1:3], 2)' mtcars.csv
```

Use `--output-indent` to change the indentation, or `0` for a single line:

```{term}
rush run -O json --output-indent 0 'head(df[1:3], 2)' mtcars.csv
```

## JSON Lines

JSON Lines has one object per line, which works well for logs and streaming:

```{term}
rush run -O jsonl 'head(df[1:3], 3)' mtcars.csv
```

```{term}
rush run -o top.jsonl 'head(df[1:3], 3)' mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' top.jsonl
```

## Nested JSON and flattening

When the output format doesn't support nesting, such as CSV, nested objects
are flattened with `jsonlite::flatten()`. Their names are joined with dots,
which become underscores when the column names are cleaned:

```{term}
echo '{"user": "alice", "meta": {"ip": "192.168.1.1", "browser": "firefox"}}
{"user": "bob", "meta": {"ip": "10.0.0.5", "browser": "chrome"}}' > logs.jsonl
rush run 'df' logs.jsonl
```

Deeper nesting is flattened too:

```{term}
echo '{"id": 1, "info": {"name": "Widget", "size": {"w": 10, "h": 5}}}
{"id": 2, "info": {"name": "Gadget", "size": {"w": 8, "h": 4}}}' > deep.jsonl
rush run 'df' deep.jsonl
```

When the output is JSON, the nesting is kept:

```{term}
rush run -O json 'df' logs.jsonl
```

## JSON with SQL

`rush sql` reads JSON and JSON Lines with DuckDB's `read_json_auto()`:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT name, age FROM people WHERE age >= 30" people.json
```

## Other extensions

Read a file with another extension as JSON with `--input-format` (`-F`):

```{term}
cp people.json people.txt
rush run -F json 'nrow(df)' people.txt
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv people.json people.txt top.jsonl logs.jsonl deep.jsonl
```
